claim_text: A person who enters or intends to enter into a transaction or agreement, called a disclosable transaction or agreement, whose principal purpose is a benefit which enables, or might be expected to enable, that person to obtain a tax advantage, shall without notice or request give the relevant tax authority information about it.

"Tax advantage" means a relief or increased relief from tax, repayment or increased repayment of tax, avoidance or reduction of a charge to tax or an assessment to tax, avoidance of a possible assessment to tax, deferral of a payment of tax or advancement of a repayment of tax, or avoidance of an obligation to deduct or account for tax.

Interest expenditure is not carried forward for more than five assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year for which the excess interest expenditure was first computed.
The limit does not apply to a Nigerian subsidiary of a foreign company which is engaged in the business of banking or insurance.

For this Schedule, debt means any loan, financial instrument, finance lease, financial derivative, or any arrangement that gives rise to interest, discounts or other finance charges that are deductible in the computation of income chargeable under the head profits and gains of business or profession.
A deduction is not allowed for any payment to a connected person that is not consistent with the Transfer Pricing Regulations issued by the Service.

claim_text: VAT that a taxable person pays to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person is called input VAT.
VAT that a taxable person collects on making taxable supplies is called output VAT.

Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, the taxable person is entitled to use the excess tax as a credit against subsequent months. This applies not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025.
A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not used as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of such information or documents as the Service may require.

Input tax on a taxable supply, including services and fixed assets, may be deducted from the tax payable on taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies.
Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted.
Input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred.
The input tax that may be deducted is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of the Act.

note: Answered: s151 non-resident rules including the s151(4) exception, s155; supported.

claim_text: Where a non-resident person makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person to whom the supply is made in Nigeria shall withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service.
A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria shall register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies.
The Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier, to collect the VAT and remit it to the Service.

Where a person appointed by the Service has made a taxable supply to a taxable person in Nigeria, the taxable person shall not have the obligation to withhold the VAT, except where the appointed person has failed to collect the VAT.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom taxable supplies are made in Nigeria and who is issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction or as may be prescribed by the Service.

The remission must be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.

A person with an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six of the Act shall keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person.

note: Answered: s187 0% for basic food items subject to para 2 of the Thirteenth Schedule; definition covers rice and garri; supported.

claim_text: Subject to paragraph 2 of the Thirtenth Schedule, basic food items are taxable supplies charged to VAT at the rate of 0%.
The general VAT rate is 7.5%, subject to the provisions of Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act.
VAT is paid on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight.

"Basic food items" means an agriculture-based or aquatic-based staple food including cereals such as rice, in the form of grain, flour or crop, whether raw or semi-processed, whether in bulk or retail.

The definition of basic food items also lists flour and starch including cassava flakes (garri), whether bleached or unbleached, refined or unrefined, provided that it is suitable for culinary purposes.

note: Answered: baby products exempt (s186(1)(d)), definition includes diapers, s186(2) proviso; supported.

claim_text: Baby products are listed among the supplies that are exempt from the VAT imposed under Chapter Six of the Act.
"Baby products" means products made for the use of babies from birth to three years of age and described in the definition.
The description of baby products includes sanitary wares, for example diapers, wipes and related products.
VAT is paid on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act.
The VAT rate of 7.5% on taxable supplies is subject to the provisions of Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act.

Despite Chapter Six, VAT is not to be collected on the items in paragraph 1 of the Eleventh Schedule, unless the Minister, by an order published in the Official Gazette, specifies a date of collection of VAT on the items listed in the order.

note: Answered: professional services excluded from small company, consulting listed; supported.

claim_text: A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

Professional services means services provided by an individual or a firm having specialised knowledge, skills, and qualifications in specific fields, including consulting, planning, or support services, excluding artisans or vocational services.
Under the Nigeria Tax Act, a small company is taxed at 0% on its total profits, and any other company at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of that Act.

note: Answered: connected persons tests for companies and the employee/client proviso; supported.

claim_text: For companies, the definition of "connected persons" includes a company that is connected to another company where the same person has control over both companies, or connected persons acting separately have control over the companies.
Two companies are also connected where one company participates directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of the other company.
Two companies are also connected where the same persons participate directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of a company and another company.

The definition says it "includes" these cases. In other cases, two persons are connected where one may reasonably be expected to act in accordance with the directions, requests, suggestions or wishes of the other.

Two persons are also connected where both may reasonably be expected to act in accordance with the directions, requests, suggestions or wishes of a third person, or where one has the practical ability to control the business decisions of the other.
Two persons are not connected solely because one is the employee or client of the other, or both are employees or clients of a third person.
"Related parties" has the same meaning as connected persons.

note: Answered: Table I Class 3 (motor vehicles) 25%, paras 6, 7 and 21; supported.

claim_text: Table I of the First Schedule, Part I lists Motor Vehicle Expenditure in Class 3, with a rate of 25%.

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, a capital allowance is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business, at the rate specified in Table I.
Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.
A capital allowance for an asset is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person is the owner of the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
An allowance is not made for a year unless it is claimed for that year, or unless the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.

note: Answered: Third Schedule 30% of EBITDA limit with the banking and insurance carve-out and five-year cap; s21(i); supported.

claim_text: Interest on debt employed in generating the income of a trade, business, profession or vocation is a deductible expense, subject to the provisions of the Third Schedule.

Where a Nigerian company or a permanent establishment of a non-resident company in Nigeria incurs interest or similar expenditure on debt issued by a connected person, the excess interest is a disallowable deduction for Chapter Two purposes.

Excess interest means total interest paid or payable to a connected person above 30% of the Nigerian company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation in that accounting period.

Interest expenditure not wholly deducted for an assessment year is carried forward to following assessment years. It is allowed against profits, if any, of any business carried on by the company and assessable for that year, to the extent permitted under paragraph (2) of the Schedule.
Interest expenditure is not carried forward for more than five assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year for which the excess interest expenditure was first computed.
The limit does not apply to a Nigerian subsidiary of a foreign company which is engaged in the business of banking or insurance.

The Schedule defines debt as any loan, financial instrument, finance lease, financial derivative, or any arrangement that gives rise to interest, discounts or other finance charges that are deductible in computing income chargeable under the head profits and gains of business or profession.
A deduction is not allowed for any payment to a connected person that is not consistent with the Transfer Pricing Regulations issued by the Service.

note: Answered: s11(5)(a) six months after the accounting year end; supported.

claim_text: For a company that has been in business for more than 18 months, the time for filing returns is not more than six months after the end of its accounting year.
This deadline is stated to be subject to the Act, any tax law or regulation.
Every company must file a self-assessment return with the Service at least once a year, whether or not it is liable to pay tax, with or without notice from the Service.
A company that permanently ceases to carry on trade or business in Nigeria must file not later than six months from the date it permanently ceases.

note: Answered: small company may attach an attested statement in place of audited accounts (s11(1)(b) proviso); supported.

claim_text: A company's self-assessment return must contain the audited financial statements, tax and capital allowances computation for the year of assessment in respect of the profit from each and every source computed.
The return of a small company may contain a statement of accounts attested to by the taxpayer in place of audited financial statements.
A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000.
A business providing professional services is not classified as a small company.

Section 11 also requires the return to contain a completed self-assessment form, evidence of payment of the tax due, a computation of the effective tax rate and additional tax payable where applicable, and an attestation signed by a principal officer of the company.

note: Answered: s36 six-year limit with the audit and deliberate misstatement exceptions; s43(4); supported.

claim_text: Where the relevant tax authority discovers or is of the opinion, at any time, that a taxable person liable to tax has not been assessed or has been assessed at less than what ought to have been charged, it may, within six years of the assessment, assess the taxable person at that amount or additional amount.
The six-year limit does not stop the relevant tax authority from continuing a tax audit and raising an additional assessment where the tax audit commenced before the six-year limit expired.

Despite the time limit in subsection (1), where there is a deliberate misstatement by a taxable person in connection with any tax imposed under the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 or any other tax law, the relevant tax authority may at any time, and as often as necessary, assess the taxable person to make good any loss of tax attributable to the deliberate misstatement.
All relevant facts are to be considered in computing the additional amount of tax, even where they were not known when a prior assessment or additional assessment was made for the same year.

Section 41 does not prevent the tax authority from making an assessment or additional assessment for any year that does not involve re-opening any issue on the same facts which was determined for that year under section 41(5) by agreement or on appeal.

note: Answered: s38 deemed profit for residents and non-residents, profit margin definition; supported.

claim_text: Where a business produces no assessable profit, or an assessable profit less than expected from that business, or the true amount of the assessable profit cannot be readily ascertained, the relevant tax authority may act under section 38.

In the case of a resident, the relevant tax authority may assess and charge that taxable person on such fair and reasonable percentage of the gross income from the trade or business as the relevant tax authority may determine.
In the case of a non-resident, the profits are the amount resulting from applying the profit margin of the person to the turnover generated from Nigeria.

Profit margin means the proportion of Earnings Before Interest and Tax (EBIT) to income or revenue in the published audited financial statement of the business. For persons not required to publish financial statements, it is the margin the relevant tax authority ascertains from financial statements of comparative companies.

note: Answered: s49(3) abeyance with the undisputed-part proviso; s49(7); supported.

claim_text: Where the taxable person has given notice of an objection or appeal, collection of tax remains in abeyance until the objection or appeal is determined, subject to section 11 of the Act.
The taxable person shall pay the tax which is not the subject of an objection or appeal.

Tax charged by an assessment that is not or has not been the subject of an objection or appeal is payable within 30 days of service of the notice of assessment, and the relevant tax authority may, in its discretion, extend that time.
Once an objection or appeal is determined, the relevant tax authority serves a notice of the tax payable as determined, and that tax is payable within 30 days of the date of service of the notice.
Where there is no objection or appeal, the relevant tax authority may proceed to enforce recovery of the tax payable in accordance with the Act.

note: Answered: s56(3) 30 days, s56(2) 12-month lapse, s55(3) 90 days; supported; a gap notes the two periods.

claim_text: Where a valid VAT refund request is received from a taxable person, the Service shall, not later than 30 days of receiving the request, refund the tax to the taxable person, or the amount shall be eligible for set-off against any tax liability of the taxpayer.
A VAT refund request is made to the Service in the prescribed form, not later than 12 months after the transaction giving rise to the refund, otherwise it shall lapse.
A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not utilised as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of such information or documents as the Service may require.

For tax refunds generally, a refund due shall be made within 90 days of the decision of the relevant tax authority made pursuant to subsection (2) of that section, with the option of a set-off against any tax liability of the taxpayer.

note: Answered: s192 arm's length duty, adjustment, definitions; supported.

claim_text: A company involved in an arrangement with a related party shall ensure that the terms and conditions of the arrangement are at arm's length.
A company involved in an arrangement with a related party shall also report the arrangement in the form and manner prescribed by the relevant tax authority.

Where, in the opinion of a relevant tax authority, a company has entered into an arrangement with a related party which is not at arm's length, the authority may make necessary adjustments to bring it into line with arm's length terms as provided under the Transfer Pricing Regulations.
The relevant tax authority may make rules or regulations for the administration of section 192.
For section 192, an "arrangement" includes any agreement, understanding, scheme, financial or commercial relation, transaction or series of transactions.
For section 192, "arm's length terms and conditions" means such terms and conditions obtainable if the transaction or arrangement was between unrelated parties dealing in comparative circumstances.

note: Answered: s66 remission; supported. Claim 2 'may also make a monthly report' is an arguable reading of s66 ('may ... remit ..., and make a monthly report'), as in tuning runs 6 and 7.

claim_text: The relevant tax authority may, for any good cause shown, remit the whole or any part of penalty or interest due under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 or any other tax law.

The relevant tax authority may also make a monthly report to the Minister or commissioner responsible for finance. The report contains details of the taxpayers, the circumstances and the amounts waived.
In the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, "relevant tax authority" means Nigeria Revenue Service, the Internal Revenue Service of a State or the Federal Capital Territory in Nigeria.

note: Answered: s56 rates, s27(1) total profits, s57 minimum ETR, s8; supported; no tax computed.

claim_text: Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%.
Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.

Total profits are the total assessable profits from all sources, including chargeable gains, less any loss ascertained in accordance with subsection (6) and capital allowance under Part I of the First Schedule.

A company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, or any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment, must recompute and pay additional tax if its effective tax rate is less than 15%, so that the rate equals 15%.

A company includes dividend income in its profits, gross of any tax paid or deducted at source. Dividends a Nigerian company receives by way of shares of the paying company are not included in its profits chargeable to tax.

note: Answered: s191(1) and (2) supported. A kept gap says the s41 passages are in Chapter Two, not Chapter Four: accurate on the context header, legal content in a kept gap (as in tuning run 7).

claim_text: Section 191 says the provisions on objections and appeals under Chapter Four of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025 apply to a direction made under that section.

Section 191 lets a relevant tax authority disregard a disposition or transaction it considers artificial or fictitious, or direct adjustments to liability to tax, and issue an assessment or additional assessment.
